newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA'S NATO INTEGRATION ON GOVERNMENT AGENDA.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA'S NATO INTEGRATION ON GOVERNMENT AGENDA.

text.p: The Romanian government on Tuesday discussed recent measures undertaken by Foreign Minister Teodor Melescanu in support of the country's bid to gain fast-track entry to NATO.

"Foreign Minister Teodor Melescanu's moves as well as President Ion Iliescu's personal messages have enjoyed a very positive impact in the United States and Canada," cabinet spokesman Ioan Rosca said, without elaborating.
Iliescu sent messages to U.S. President Bill Clinton and Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien to restate Romania's bid to be allowed into the Western defence alliance in any first wave of admission.
Similar messages are expected to be delievered to leaders of all NATO member countries.
Rosca said Romania had been praised abroad for its rapid ratification of a frienship treaty with neighbouring Hungary, as well as its signature of a treaty with Yugoslavia.
"We expect the Romanian-Hungarian treaty to be fully ratified by the end of the year, with the Hungarian parliament to debate ratification in an emergency procedure," Rosca said.
Other items on the cabinet's agenda on Tuesday included:
* report on autumn harvest, saying 65 percent of sunflower harvest was completed, while only 41 percent of maize has been harvested
* decision to sow 1.9 million hectares under wheat for 1997
* decision to put at 14.8 million cubic metres the 1997 timber quota, of which some 120,000 would be up for export
* measures to build stocks of up to 7.8 million tonnes of coal and some 700,000 tonnes of fuel oil for Romania's special winter energy reserves. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
